label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
Hi Mikaela, sorry it's taken me a few days, I'm hopeless typing on this thing. Least I can do after everything you did for us when Dave did his shoulder. Real version, not the brochure:

We've got 290 cows, mostly 3-way crosses, and started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept once mating had started. We skip the arvo milking Tues, Thurs, Sat and Sun, so four once-a-days a week. Mornings are still 5.15 every day, that part doesn't change.

Production first. Milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep had told us to expect 8 to 10, so it's been better than we were warned.

Cells, yes they jumped. We went from 110k to about 180k in the first three weeks. They're back around 135k now, so settled but still a bit above where we started.

The bad bit you need to hear. We had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo. Nobody spotted it till the next morning and she lost a quarter. That's the risk with it, there's a much longer gap where nobody's got eyes on them. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and checking cows on the skip days or it bites you. If the plan is that arvos off means nobody looks at the herd, I wouldn't do it.

Good bits. Lameness is way down, 4 on the lame list now against 11 this time last year. Our walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km, so four fewer trips a week has made a real difference. The cows came round quicker than I thought too, about four days of bellowing at the gate and then they were fine.

The people side is the big one for us though. The first Sunday arvo we skipped, Dave and I drove to Hamilton to see the grandkids. First Sunday off in spring in 20 odd years. And Kieran our 2IC said it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October, which might be worth thinking about with your young fella. If Tom's knees are stuffed, the arvos off will help him more than anything else.

Honestly, we wouldn't go back. The hours alone are worth the 6% to us. But that's our farm, and we started in September where you'd be starting after Christmas, so I can't promise your numbers will look like ours. I don't want you cursing me in March!

I'll bring our shed rosters and the numbers to the field day on the 19th so you can have a proper look. Grant, you're welcome to have a nosy too. Or just ring me Mikaela, much easier than texting.
